items.title: Beyond vibe coding: Mastering the AI-native SDLC from code to production
items.reason: Starts with the engineering discipline Priya cares about: using AI across planning, coding, testing, modernization and deployment while preserving quality, security and control—directly relevant to shipping GenAI features beyond prototypes.
items.question: Where do you recommend inserting objective eval gates in an AI-native SDLC so AI-generated code cannot move from prototype to production on vibes alone?

items.title: Your Agent Stack Is Broken at the Bottom
items.reason: Targets the data-layer bottlenecks that production agents hit: concurrency, real-time access patterns, scale and cost—useful for agent systems serving fintech workloads.
items.question: For autonomous agents issuing machine-speed queries, what workload signal tells you the database layer is becoming the bottleneck before customer-facing latency or cost spikes?

items.title: From AI Demos to Production: What It Really Takes to Build Enterprise-Ready AI - Moving beyond POCs into architecture, reliability, evaluation, security and scale.
items.reason: A near-perfect match for Priya’s production focus: reliability, evaluation, security, guardrails, right-sized LLMs and cost/accuracy/throughput trade-offs after the POC stage.
items.question: When balancing throughput, accuracy and cost with right-sized LLMs, what evaluation design best detects regressions caused by model or prompt changes in production?

items.title: Lunch
items.reason: Protected lunch block in Hall 3; it avoids Priya’s 14:00–15:00 sprint review call and keeps the afternoon clash-free.

items.title: The Missing Infrastructure Behind India’s AI Ambition
items.reason: Gives a data-infrastructure view of model-ready, representative, consented data—important for robust India-scale LLM products and multilingual fintech experiences.
items.question: How would you measure whether an Indic/code-switched dataset is truly model-ready for reliability-sensitive agent workflows rather than merely large?

items.title: Build with Bob: It's More Than Just a Vibe
items.reason: Hands-on developer workshop for AI-powered app building, API integration, debugging and modernization—good practical exposure after the morning SDLC talks.
items.question: In the lab workflow, what guardrails or review steps prevent AI-assisted modernization from introducing subtle API-contract or security regressions?

items.title: Agent Harness for Enterprise: Engineering the Runtime for Reliable AI Agents
items.reason: Priya’s must-attend and the deepest fit: enterprise agent runtime architecture covering skill discovery, context compaction, delegation, verification loops, identity, observability and governance.
items.question: For a fintech agent that can execute tools, which verification loop and identity-propagation pattern would you make mandatory before allowing high-risk actions?

items.title: The Agentic Platform: Powering Operations for Real Business Outcomes
items.reason: Shows how to move agentic AI from experiments into responsible, scalable operations with orchestration, context, enterprise integration and governance.
items.question: What platform primitive should teams standardize first—context, orchestration, integration or governance—if they want measurable outcomes without locking themselves into one agent framework?

items.title: AI can build almost anything. What should we build?
items.reason: Addresses the economics Priya flagged: lower build cost, hidden model dependency costs, token economics and using judgment to avoid shipping low-value AI work.
items.question: How do you quantify the opportunity cost of building an AI feature fast when proprietary data, model dependency and token economics are still uncertain?

items.title: Lunch
items.reason: Lunch after Priya’s 11:00–13:00 booth duty; leaves enough time to move to the 14:30 Hall 2 session.

items.title: Beyond Agents: Building Systems of Enterprise Intelligence
items.reason: Connects isolated agents to coordinated enterprise intelligence, focusing on coordination tax, economics and intelligence yield—key for multi-agent production architecture.
items.question: What metric have you found most useful for detecting Coordination Tax when several agents pursue competing objectives across enterprise workflows?

items.title: Building Voice AI from India, for India, and for the world
items.reason: Useful for production AI interfaces at India scale: multilingual support, code-switching, accents, noisy settings, real-time constraints and cost-effective infrastructure.
items.question: For multilingual, code-switched voice AI, which reliability metric best captures failures that standard word-error-rate hides in real customer interactions?

items.title: Operations + AI: Beyond Automation: Reimagining Supply Chains, Manufacturing and Operations with AI
items.reason: Broadens Priya’s production lens from model behavior to operating models: sensing, predicting, deciding and scaling AI beyond pilots with measurable business value.
items.question: When moving from isolated AI use cases to an integrated operating model, how do you prevent local automations from optimizing against the global business outcome?

items.title: Agentic Data Cloud: From building the analytics data foundation with Knowledge Catalog, federating it with transactional data to generating advanced insights using Agentic Intelligence.
items.reason: Hands-on workshop on knowledge catalogs, data federation and data agents—directly relevant to building grounded, enterprise-grade agents over transactional data.
items.question: In the hands-on architecture, how do you enforce lineage and access controls when a data agent federates cataloged analytics data with live transactional sources?

items.title: How to Build Your Enterprise AI Stack
items.reason: Frames the full AI stack—models, data, compute, infrastructure, talent and applications—helping Priya place agent engineering choices in a broader enterprise architecture.
items.question: For an Indian fintech startup, which layer of the enterprise AI stack is most dangerous to outsource too early: data, models, evaluation infrastructure, or deployment runtime?

items.title: Consuming AI at Scale: Lessons from a Regulated Industry
items.reason: Direct fintech relevance: integrating third-party AI in banking operations while balancing innovation with regulatory obligations.
items.question: What due-diligence evidence should a regulated bank require before allowing a third-party AI component into a customer-impacting workflow?

items.title: Secure Your Agentic Future: No More Rogue Agents
items.reason: Matches Priya’s secure-agent interest with a practical blueprint for discovering, onboarding, protecting and governing agents in sensitive environments.
items.question: How should agent identity and lifecycle management differ from human/service-account IAM when agents can dynamically discover tools and act autonomously?

items.title: Crash. Resume. Repeat: Building Agents That Don't Die
items.reason: Deep production reliability fit: durable execution for multi-step agents that survive crashes, retries, timeouts and partial progress without losing state.
items.question: How do you design idempotency and compensation when a resumed agent must avoid re-running a tool call that already succeeded but produced an external side effect?

items.title: The Agent Economy: Who owns the customer when the agent is the interface?
items.reason: Satisfies the panel requirement and is strategically relevant to fintech: if agents choose cards, products or merchants, ownership of the customer and transaction becomes a core product risk.
items.question: In the banking example, what disclosure or control should be mandatory when an agent selects a payment instrument on behalf of a user?

items.title: Lunch
items.reason: Lunch immediately after the Hall 1 panel; keeps the afternoon schedule relaxed and leaves enough walking time for the later Hall 3 workshop.

items.title: The Trust Deficit: Building Responsible AI in a Regulated, Risk-Heavy Business
items.reason: Strong fintech fit: covers responsible AI, explainability, oversight, bias mitigation, governance and human accountability in financial services.
items.question: Which responsible-AI control is most often missing when financial institutions move from compliance documentation to AI systems that are trustworthy by design?

items.title: From Idea to Production: Build Enterprise-Grade Applications with Agentic AI
items.reason: Final hands-on workshop before Priya leaves for her flight: practical agentic AI development with app building, API work, debugging and production-oriented workflows.
items.question: During the workshop, where would you add automated tests or eval harnesses so AI-assisted development produces production-grade applications rather than just faster demos?

summary: A production-agent-heavy agenda for Priya: 19 non-lunch sessions across all 3 days, including 4 workshops and 1 panel. The plan avoids her sprint review, booth duty and flight cutoff, includes lunch daily, preserves 5-minute hall-switching buffers, and emphasizes agent harnesses, reliability, governance, evaluation, data foundations, security and AI economics.
